bio.fr: Ancien pilote de la RAF, il devient Premier ministre de la Rhodésie du Sud en 1964. En 1965, il proclame unilatéralement l'indépendance pour maintenir le pouvoir de la minorité blanche, malgré les sanctions de l'ONU. La guerre contre les mouvements nationalistes noirs fait des dizaines de milliers de morts avant les accords de Lancaster House en 1979.
bio.en: A former RAF pilot, he became prime minister of Southern Rhodesia in 1964. In 1965 he unilaterally declared independence to preserve white minority rule, defying UN sanctions. The war against Black nationalist movements killed tens of thousands before the Lancaster House Agreement of 1979.

bio.fr: Militaire nommé Premier ministre, il écarte Habib Bourguiba pour sénilité en novembre 1987 et prend la présidence de la Tunisie. Son régime autoritaire, marqué par la répression et la corruption, dure 23 ans. Après l'immolation de Mohamed Bouazizi, la révolution le pousse à fuir en Arabie saoudite en janvier 2011.
bio.en: A military man appointed prime minister, he removed Habib Bourguiba on grounds of senility in November 1987 and took over as president of Tunisia. His authoritarian rule, marked by repression and corruption, lasted 23 years. After Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire, the revolution drove him to flee to Saudi Arabia in January 2011.

bio.fr: Ancien commandant de l'armée, il renverse Hissène Habré en 1990 et dirige le Tchad pendant plus de trente ans. Il fait de son armée un acteur majeur de la lutte contre les groupes djihadistes au Sahel. Il meurt en 2021 lors de combats contre des rebelles, et son fils lui succède.
bio.en: A former army commander, he overthrew Hissène Habré in 1990 and ruled Chad for more than three decades. He made his army a major force against jihadist groups in the Sahel. He died in 2021 during fighting with rebels, and his son took over.

bio.fr: Officier du Derg, la junte qui renverse Haïlé Sélassié en 1974, il s'impose à sa tête et dirige l'Éthiopie jusqu'en 1991. Sa « Terreur rouge » de 1977-1978 fait des dizaines de milliers de morts, et ses réinstallations forcées aggravent la famine de 1983-1985, qui tue environ un million de personnes. Réfugié au Zimbabwe, il est condamné à mort par contumace pour génocide en 2008.
bio.en: An officer of the Derg, the junta that toppled Haile Selassie in 1974, he rose to lead it and ruled Ethiopia until 1991. His Red Terror of 1977–78 killed tens of thousands, and his forced resettlements worsened the 1983–85 famine, which killed around a million people. Sheltering in Zimbabwe, he was sentenced to death in absentia for genocide in 2008.

bio.fr: Avocate, elle est ministre des Affaires étrangères du Venezuela de 2014 à 2017 puis préside l'Assemblée constituante. Vice-présidente de Nicolás Maduro à partir de 2018, elle cumule des fonctions clés dans l'économie et le pétrole. Elle assure la présidence par intérim après la capture de Maduro par les États-Unis en janvier 2026.
bio.en: A lawyer, she was Venezuela's foreign minister from 2014 to 2017 and then presided over the Constituent Assembly. As Nicolás Maduro's vice president from 2018, she also held key economic and oil portfolios. She became acting president after the United States captured Maduro in January 2026.

bio.fr: Chef du Front populaire de libération de l'Érythrée, il conduit la guerre d'indépendance contre l'Éthiopie et dirige le pays depuis 1991. Aucune élection présidentielle n'a eu lieu, et la Constitution adoptée en 1997 n'est jamais entrée en vigueur. Son régime impose un service national à durée indéterminée qui pousse de nombreux jeunes à l'exil.
bio.en: Leader of the Eritrean People's Liberation Front, he led the independence war against Ethiopia and has ruled the country since 1991. No presidential election has ever been held, and the constitution adopted in 1997 has never taken effect. His government enforces open-ended national service that has driven many young people into exile.

bio.fr: Ingénieur formé en Union soviétique et cadre du MPLA, il succède à Agostinho Neto en 1979 et dirige l’Angola pendant 38 ans. Sa présidence traverse une longue guerre civile contre l’UNITA, achevée en 2002, puis un boom pétrolier qui enrichit surtout le cercle du pouvoir et sa famille.
bio.en: A Soviet-trained engineer and MPLA official, he took over from Agostinho Neto in 1979 and ruled Angola for 38 years. His tenure spanned a long civil war against UNITA that ended in 2002, followed by an oil boom whose wealth flowed largely to the ruling circle and his own family.

bio.en: Governor of Santa Cruz province, he won the presidency in 2003 while Argentina was still reeling from the 2001 crash. He restructured the debt, paid off the IMF in 2006 and reopened trials of the dictatorship's officers, then handed over to his wife Cristina in 2007.

bio.fr: Commandant de l’armée, il renverse Isabel Perón en mars 1976 et préside la junte jusqu’en 1981. Sous son régime, la « guerre sale » fait disparaître des milliers d’opposants, jusqu’à 30 000 selon les organisations de droits humains, torturés dans des centres clandestins, et des centaines de bébés sont volés à des détenues. Condamné à perpétuité en 1985, gracié en 1990, il est de nouveau condamné et meurt en prison en 2013.
bio.en: As army commander he overthrew Isabel Perón in March 1976 and led the junta until 1981. Under his rule the Dirty War made thousands of opponents disappear, up to 30,000 according to human rights groups, many tortured in secret detention centres, while hundreds of babies were taken from imprisoned mothers. Sentenced to life in 1985 and pardoned in 1990, he was convicted again and died in prison in 2013.

bio.fr: Issu d’une famille modeste de la vallée du Rift, il devient vice-président d’Uhuru Kenyatta en 2013 alors que la CPI le poursuit pour les violences post-électorales de 2007-2008, charges abandonnées en 2016. Se présentant comme le champion des « débrouillards », il remporte la présidentielle de 2022.
bio.en: Raised in modest circumstances in the Rift Valley, he became Uhuru Kenyatta's deputy president in 2013 while facing ICC charges over the 2007–2008 post-election violence, a case dropped in 2016. Campaigning as the champion of ordinary hustlers, he won the 2022 presidential election.

bio.fr: Porté au pouvoir par la révolution de 1930, il instaure en 1937 l’Estado Novo, un régime autoritaire et centralisateur qui crée aussi un droit du travail. Écarté par l’armée en 1945, il revient par les urnes en 1951, puis se suicide au palais présidentiel en 1954 en pleine crise politique.
bio.en: Brought to power by the 1930 revolution, he set up the Estado Novo in 1937, an authoritarian, centralising regime that also introduced labour laws. Removed by the army in 1945, he returned through the ballot box in 1951 and shot himself in the presidential palace in 1954 amid a political crisis.

bio.fr: Héritier de la chefferie bamangwato, il est exilé par les autorités britanniques après son mariage avec une Anglaise, Ruth Williams. Revenu en politique, il conduit le Botswana à l’indépendance en 1966 et le préside jusqu’à sa mort, en gérant les revenus du diamant de façon prudente et démocratique.
bio.en: Heir to the Bamangwato chieftaincy, he was exiled by the British after marrying an Englishwoman, Ruth Williams. Back in politics, he led Botswana to independence in 1966 and governed until his death, steering the new diamond revenues with notable prudence inside a working democracy.

bio.fr: Longtemps trésorier dans les gouvernements Menzies, il lui succède en 1966 à la tête du Parti libéral et du pays. Il engage davantage l’Australie au Viêt Nam et organise le référendum de 1967 sur les Aborigènes, avant de disparaître en mer en se baignant près de Portsea en décembre 1967.
bio.en: After years as Treasurer under Robert Menzies, he succeeded him as Liberal leader and prime minister in 1966. He deepened Australia's commitment in Vietnam and held the 1967 referendum on Aboriginal Australians, then vanished while swimming off Cheviot Beach in December 1967.

Emprisonné sous Nasser, il rédige des ouvrages dénonçant les sociétés musulmanes jugées impies, dont « Jalons sur la route », qui inspireront l’islamisme radical. Il est pendu en 1966.
bio.en: An Egyptian writer and civil servant, he joined the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1950s and became its leading thinker. Jailed under Nasser, he wrote works condemning Muslim societies he saw as ungodly, notably Milestones, which later shaped radical Islamist movements. He was hanged in 1966.

En novembre 1975, le gouverneur général John Kerr le révoque, un fait sans précédent dans l’histoire australienne.
bio.en: He brought Labor back to power in 1972 after 23 years in opposition and pushed through a burst of reforms: ending conscription, recognising China and creating universal health insurance. In November 1975 Governor-General John Kerr dismissed him, an event without precedent in Australian history.

bio.fr: Fils de l’opposant historique Étienne Tshisekedi, il prend la tête de l’UDPS et est proclamé vainqueur de la présidentielle de 2018, une élection contestée. Son investiture en 2019 marque la première passation de pouvoir pacifique du pays ; il est réélu en 2023 alors que la guerre se poursuit dans l’Est.
bio.en: Son of veteran opposition leader Étienne Tshisekedi, he took over the UDPS and was declared winner of the disputed 2018 presidential election. His 2019 inauguration was the country's first peaceful handover of power, and he was re-elected in 2023 as fighting continued in the east.

À sa mort en juillet 1974, elle devient la première femme présidente d’une république au monde, mais son gouvernement sombre dans la crise et la violence politique jusqu’au coup d’État de mars 1976.
bio.en: A dancer who became Juan Perón's third wife, she was elected his vice president in 1973. On his death in July 1974 she became the world's first woman president of a republic, but her government sank into economic crisis and political violence until the military coup of March 1976.

Renversé par Idi Amin en 1971, il revient au pouvoir en 1980 ; sa lutte contre la guérilla de Museveni s’accompagne de massacres de civils, notamment dans le triangle de Luwero, avant un nouveau coup d’État en 1985.
bio.en: Prime minister at independence in 1962, he seized full power in 1966 and abolished the traditional kingdoms. Overthrown by Idi Amin in 1971, he returned in 1980, and his war against Museveni's guerrillas brought mass killings of civilians, notably in the Luwero Triangle, before another coup removed him in 1985.

bio.en: A son of Huayna Capac, he defeated his half-brother Huáscar in the succession war that split the empire. Seized by Francisco Pizarro at Cajamarca in 1532, he had a room filled with gold and silver as his ransom, yet the Spaniards executed him in 1533.

Battu par Adama Barrow en 2016, il refuse d’abord sa défaite puis s’exile en Guinée équatoriale en 2017 sous la pression de la CEDEAO.
bio.en: A young lieutenant, he seized power in a 1994 coup and ruled the Gambia for 22 years through fear, with opponents disappeared and tortured. Defeated by Adama Barrow in 2016, he first refused to concede, then left for exile in Equatorial Guinea in 2017 under pressure from West African troops.

bio.en: A former currency trader at Merrill Lynch, he took over the National Party and became prime minister in 2008. He steered the country through the financial crisis and the rebuilding after the Christchurch earthquakes, held two referendums on the flag, and stepped down unexpectedly in 2016.

bio.en: A general at the heart of several coups, he seized power in 1993 and ruled Nigeria with an iron grip until his death in 1998. His regime jailed opponents, hanged the writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight Ogoni activists in 1995, and siphoned off billions of dollars.

bio.en: Chief wife of Ramesses II, she held a prominent place at court and in diplomacy with the Hittites, as her letters to Queen Puduhepa show. The pharaoh dedicated a temple to her at Abu Simbel, and her tomb in the Valley of the Queens is among the finest in Egypt.

bio.en: An academic and Labour stalwart, she became New Zealand's first elected woman prime minister in 1999 and held the post for nine years. She kept the country out of the Iraq war, then led the United Nations Development Programme from 2009 to 2017.

bio.en: A schoolteacher turned independence leader, he was Zambia's first president from 1964 to 1991. He imposed one-party rule in 1972 and backed liberation movements across southern Africa, then accepted defeat by Frederick Chiluba when multiparty elections returned in 1991.

bio.en: Elected in 1990 after the assassination of Luis Carlos Galán, whose campaign he had been running, he oversaw the adoption of the 1991 Constitution. His term was dominated by the hunt for Pablo Escobar, killed in 1993, after which he became Secretary General of the Organization of American States.

bio.en: A Peronist governor of La Rioja, he was elected president in 1989 in the middle of hyperinflation. He pegged the peso to the dollar, privatised on a vast scale and pardoned the junta leaders, while his model ended in the 2001 crash two years after he left office.

bio.en: A lawyer serving as Pedro Castillo's vice president, she replaced him in December 2022 after his attempt to dissolve Congress. The crackdown on the ensuing protests left dozens dead, and her deeply unpopular presidency ended when Congress removed her in 2025.

bio.en: A rural schoolteacher and union leader, he narrowly won the 2021 presidential election for the left-wing Perú Libre party. In December 2022 he tried to dissolve Congress, was removed from office that same day, and was arrested and prosecuted for rebellion.

Son gouvernement de transition est marqué par des répressions meurtrières à Sacaba et Senkata ; elle est condamnée en 2022 à dix ans de prison.
bio.en: A right-wing senator, she declared herself interim president in November 2019 after Evo Morales resigned under pressure from protesters and the military. Her caretaker government saw deadly crackdowns at Sacaba and Senkata, and in 2022 she was sentenced to ten years in prison.

bio.en: A general who seized power in a 1954 coup, he ruled Paraguay for 35 years through the Colorado Party. His regime jailed, tortured and disappeared opponents, joined Operation Condor and sheltered former Nazis, until he was overthrown in 1989.

bio.en: Heir to a banana fortune, he was elected in 2023 at the age of 35, one of the youngest presidents in Ecuador's history. Confronting a surge in cartel violence, he declared an internal armed conflict in 2024 and won re-election in 2025.

bio.en: An economist, he served as Evo Morales's economy minister through more than a decade of strong growth. Elected president for MAS in 2020, he fell out with Morales and faced shortages of dollars and fuel before leaving office in 2025.

bio.en: A Peruvian diplomat, he was UN Secretary-General from 1982 to 1991. He brokered the 1988 ceasefire between Iran and Iraq and helped wind down several Cold War conflicts, later serving briefly as Peru's prime minister after Fujimori's fall.

bio.en: An economist who worked at the World Bank and served as a minister in several governments, he narrowly beat Keiko Fujimori for the presidency in 2016. Weakened by a hostile Congress and ties to Odebrecht, he resigned in March 2018 after videos of vote-buying surfaced.

bio.en: As army commander he became head of the military junta in December 1981. In April 1982 he ordered the invasion of the Falkland Islands to rally support for the regime, and defeat by Britain in June forced him out and hastened the end of the dictatorship.

bio.en: The illegitimate son of an Irish-born viceroy of Peru, he fought for Chilean independence and won at Chacabuco alongside San Martín in 1817. As Supreme Director until 1823 he proclaimed independence in 1818, then, facing opposition, spent his last years in exile in Peru.

bio.en: A wheelchair user since being shot in a 1998 robbery, he served as Rafael Correa's vice president and succeeded him in 2017. He soon broke with his mentor, moved closer to the United States and faced mass protests in 2019 over the end of fuel subsidies.

bio.en: A gifted APRA orator, he became president in 1985 at 36, but his first term ended in hyperinflation amid Shining Path violence. Re-elected in 2006, he oversaw strong growth, and in 2019 he took his own life as police arrived to arrest him in the Odebrecht case.

bio.en: A lawyer and former congressman, he left the UDI to found the Republican Party in 2019 on the Chilean hard right. Beaten by Gabriel Boric in 2021, he won the 2025 presidential election on a platform focused on crime and immigration, taking office in March 2026.

bio.en: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, a local chief descended from the last Incas, took the name Túpac Amaru II and in 1780 launched the largest uprising against Spanish rule in the Andes. Captured, he was executed in Cuzco in 1781 along with much of his family.

bio.en: An oncologist and former mayor of Montevideo, he became the first Frente Amplio president in 2005, ending the long dominance of Uruguay's traditional parties. Elected again for 2015 to 2020, he championed pioneering anti-smoking laws.

bio.en: A former governor of Antioquia, he was elected in 2002 and again in 2006 on a hard line against the FARC known as Democratic Security. His offensive badly weakened the guerrillas, but his years in office were stained by the false positives scandal, in which the army killed civilians and passed them off as rebels.

bio.en: Ruling as regent for his mother, he fled Napoleon's invasion in 1807 and moved the Portuguese court to Rio de Janeiro. He raised Brazil to a kingdom in 1815 and became king in 1816, then returned to Lisbon in 1821, shortly before his son Pedro declared Brazil independent.

bio.fr: Sociologue exilé sous la dictature, il devient ministre des Finances en 1993 et lance le plan Real, qui met fin à l’hyperinflation. Élu président en 1994 puis réélu, il gouverne de 1995 à 2002 en stabilisant l’économie et en privatisant de grandes entreprises publiques.
bio.en: A sociologist forced into exile under the dictatorship, he became finance minister in 1993 and launched the Real Plan, which ended hyperinflation. Elected president in 1994 and re-elected, he governed from 1995 to 2002, stabilising the economy and privatising major state firms.

bio.fr: Urbaniste de formation et ancien ministre du Logement, il devient président en 2020 après une longue bataille électorale. Il gère l’arrivée massive de revenus pétroliers offshore et défend la région de l’Essequibo face aux revendications du Venezuela, avant d’être réélu en 2025.
bio.en: A trained urban planner and former housing minister, he became president in 2020 after a drawn-out election dispute. He has managed the influx of offshore oil revenue and defended the Essequibo region against Venezuela's claims, winning re-election in 2025.

bio.fr: Sergent-chef, il mène le coup d’État de 1980 et domine le Suriname dans les années 1980 ; en décembre 1982, quinze opposants sont exécutés sur ses ordres. Revenu au pouvoir par les urnes de 2010 à 2020, il est condamné pour ces meurtres et meurt en 2024 alors qu’il se soustrait à sa peine.
bio.en: A sergeant major, he led the 1980 coup and dominated Suriname through the 1980s, and in December 1982 fifteen opponents were executed on his orders. Elected president from 2010 to 2020, he was convicted of those killings and died in 2024 while evading his sentence.

bio.fr: Médecin et ancien gouverneur du Minas Gerais, il préside le Brésil de 1956 à 1961 avec la promesse de « cinquante ans de progrès en cinq ». Il industrialise le pays et fait construire Brasília, la nouvelle capitale inaugurée en 1960, au prix d’une forte dette.
bio.en: A physician and former governor of Minas Gerais, he led Brazil from 1956 to 1961, promising fifty years of progress in five. He drove industrialisation and built Brasília, the new capital inaugurated in 1960, at the cost of heavy borrowing.

role.en: Sapa Inca of the Inca Empire

bio.fr: Après avoir repoussé une attaque des Chancas contre Cuzco, il prend le pouvoir vers 1438 et transforme un petit royaume andin en vaste empire, le Tawantinsuyu. On lui attribue la reconstruction de Cuzco et la fondation du domaine royal de Machu Picchu.
bio.en: After driving back a Chanka assault on Cuzco, he took power around 1438 and turned a small Andean kingdom into a vast empire, Tawantinsuyu. He is credited with rebuilding Cuzco and founding the royal estate of Machu Picchu.

description.fr: +3 en Stratégie contre une carte du Moyen Âge.
description.en: +3 Strategy against a Medieval card.

bio.fr: Héritier politique de Getúlio Vargas, il est vice-président puis accède à la présidence en 1961 après la démission de Jânio Quadros. Ses « réformes de base », dont une réforme agraire, inquiètent l’armée et les milieux conservateurs, qui le renversent en 1964 ; il meurt en exil en Argentine en 1976.
bio.en: Political heir to Getúlio Vargas, he was vice president and took over in 1961 when Jânio Quadros resigned. His basic reforms, including land reform, alarmed the military and conservatives, who overthrew him in 1964, and he died in exile in Argentina in 1976.

bio.fr: Avocat de l’Union civique radicale, il est élu en 1983 et ramène la démocratie après la dictature. Il crée la commission CONADEP sur les disparus et fait juger les chefs de la junte en 1985, mais l’hyperinflation le pousse à transmettre le pouvoir de manière anticipée en 1989.
bio.en: A Radical Civic Union lawyer, he was elected in 1983 and restored democracy after the dictatorship. He set up the CONADEP commission on the disappeared and put the junta leaders on trial in 1985, but hyperinflation led him to hand over power early in 1989.

bio.fr: Ingénieur et ancien gouverneur de Moquegua, il succède à Pedro Pablo Kuczynski en 2018. Populaire pour sa lutte affichée contre la corruption, il dissout le Congrès en 2019, mais le nouveau Parlement le destitue en novembre 2020 pour « incapacité morale ».
bio.en: An engineer and former governor of Moquegua, he succeeded Pedro Pablo Kuczynski in 2018. Popular for his anti-corruption stance, he dissolved Congress in 2019, but the new legislature removed him in November 2020 on grounds of moral incapacity.

bio.fr: Officier de l’armée, il mène en 2000 un soulèvement contre le régime d’Alberto Fujimori, puis fonde un parti nationaliste. Élu président en 2011, il gouverne au centre jusqu’en 2016 avant d’être rattrapé avec son épouse par des poursuites sur le financement de ses campagnes.
bio.en: An army officer, he led a 2000 uprising against Alberto Fujimori's regime and went on to found a nationalist party. Elected president in 2011, he governed from the centre until 2016, after which he and his wife faced prosecution over the funding of his campaigns.

role.fr: Généralissime de la Première République du Venezuela
role.en: Generalissimo of the First Republic of Venezuela

bio.fr: Officier vénézuélien, il combat dans la guerre d’indépendance américaine puis dans les armées de la Révolution française, où son nom figure sur l’Arc de triomphe. Précurseur de l’indépendance hispano-américaine, il dirige la Première République en 1812, capitule et meurt prisonnier à Cadix en 1816.
bio.en: A Venezuelan officer, he fought in the American War of Independence and then in the armies of the French Revolution, earning his name on the Arc de Triomphe. A forerunner of Spanish American independence, he led the First Republic in 1812, surrendered and died a prisoner in Cádiz in 1816.

bio.fr: Ancien chef de la police, il dirige l’enquête sur les meurtres de décembre 1982 imputés à Desi Bouterse. Chef du parti VHP, il est élu président en 2020 et engage un programme d’austérité face à la crise de la dette, avant de céder la place en 2025.
bio.en: A former police commissioner, he led the investigation into the December 1982 killings attributed to Desi Bouterse. As head of the VHP party he became president in 2020 and imposed austerity to tackle a debt crisis before stepping down in 2025.

bio.fr: Bras droit de Simón Bolívar, il remporte les batailles de Pichincha en 1822 et d’Ayacucho en 1824, qui scellent l’indépendance de l’Amérique du Sud espagnole. Premier président de la Bolivie, il quitte le pays en 1828, puis est assassiné dans une embuscade en Colombie en 1830.
bio.en: Simón Bolívar's right-hand man, he won the battles of Pichincha in 1822 and Ayacucho in 1824, which sealed the independence of Spanish South America. He became Bolivia's first president, left the country in 1828 and was killed in an ambush in Colombia in 1830.

bio.fr: Jeune gouverneur d’Alagoas, il devient en 1989 le premier président élu au suffrage direct depuis la dictature. Son plan contre l’inflation gèle l’épargne des Brésiliens, puis un scandale de corruption entraîne une procédure de destitution et sa démission en décembre 1992.
bio.en: A young governor of Alagoas, he became in 1989 the first president chosen by direct vote since the dictatorship. His anti-inflation plan froze Brazilians' savings, and a corruption scandal led to impeachment proceedings and his resignation in December 1992.

bio.fr: Fils de l’ancien président Luis Alberto Lacalle, il mène le Parti national à la victoire en 2019 et met fin à quinze ans de gouvernements du Frente Amplio. Président de 2020 à 2025, il gère la pandémie en misant sur la « liberté responsable » plutôt que sur le confinement obligatoire.
bio.en: Son of former president Luis Alberto Lacalle, he led the National Party to victory in 2019, ending fifteen years of Frente Amplio rule. President from 2020 to 2025, he handled the pandemic through what he called responsible freedom rather than mandatory lockdowns.

bio.fr: Figure de l’Union civique radicale, il est le premier chef de gouvernement élu de la ville de Buenos Aires en 1996, puis président en 1999. Englué dans la récession, il laisse imposer le « corralito » qui gèle les dépôts et démissionne en décembre 2001 au milieu d’émeutes meurtrières.
bio.en: A leading Radical, he became the first elected head of government of the city of Buenos Aires in 1996 and president in 1999. Mired in recession, his government imposed the corralito freezing bank deposits, and he resigned in December 2001 amid deadly riots.

role.fr: Chef du Sentier lumineux au Pérou
role.en: Leader of the Shining Path in Peru

bio.fr: Professeur de philosophie maoïste, il fonde le Sentier lumineux et déclenche en 1980 une insurrection armée contre l’État péruvien. Le conflit fait environ 70 000 morts, dont près de la moitié attribuée à son organisation, qui pratique massacres de paysans, comme à Lucanamarca en 1983, et attentats à la bombe. Capturé en 1992, il est condamné à la perpétuité et meurt en prison en 2021.
bio.en: A Maoist philosophy professor, he founded the Shining Path and launched an armed insurgency against the Peruvian state in 1980. The conflict killed around 70,000 people, nearly half of them attributed to his movement, which massacred peasants, as at Lucanamarca in 1983, and carried out bombings. Captured in 1992, he was sentenced to life and died in prison in 2021.

description.en: -2 Diplomacy to the opposing card in round 1.

role.fr: Gouverneur de la province de Buenos Aires

bio.fr: Riche estanciero et chef fédéraliste, il gouverne Buenos Aires de 1829 à 1832 puis de 1835 à 1852 avec des pouvoirs absolus, dirigeant de fait la Confédération argentine. Sa police politique, la Mazorca, terrorise les opposants unitaires ; battu à Caseros en 1852, il meurt en exil en Angleterre.
bio.en: A wealthy rancher and Federalist leader, he governed Buenos Aires from 1829 to 1832 and again from 1835 to 1852 with absolute powers, acting as de facto ruler of the Argentine Confederation. His political police, the Mazorca, terrorised Unitarian opponents, and after defeat at Caseros in 1852 he died in exile in England.

bio.fr: Ancien fonctionnaire de la Banque interaméricaine de développement et protégé d’Álvaro Uribe, il est élu en 2018 à 42 ans. Critique de l’accord de paix avec les FARC, il affronte la pandémie puis la grève nationale de 2021, réprimée avec violence.
bio.en: A former Inter-American Development Bank official and protégé of Álvaro Uribe, he was elected in 2018 at the age of 42. A critic of the peace deal with the FARC, he faced the pandemic and then the 2021 national strike, which was violently repressed.

bio.fr: Avocat médiatique connu pour avoir défendu des clients controversés, il se lance en politique comme candidat indépendant de droite. Il fait campagne pour la présidentielle colombienne de 2026 sur un discours de fermeté face au crime et aux groupes armés.
bio.en: A high-profile lawyer known for defending controversial clients, he entered politics as an independent right-wing candidate. He ran in Colombia's 2026 presidential election on a tough-on-crime message aimed at armed groups.

bio.fr: Fils et successeur de Carlos Antonio López, il dirige le Paraguay à partir de 1862. Il entraîne le pays dans la guerre de la Triple-Alliance contre le Brésil, l’Argentine et l’Uruguay, qui coûte au Paraguay une grande partie de sa population, et meurt au combat à Cerro Corá en 1870.
bio.en: Son and successor of Carlos Antonio López, he ruled Paraguay from 1862. He led the country into the War of the Triple Alliance against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, which cost Paraguay a large share of its population, and was killed in battle at Cerro Corá in 1870.

bio.fr: Homme d’affaires enrichi notamment dans le tabac, il entre en politique tardivement et ramène le Parti colorado au pouvoir en 2013. Président jusqu’en 2018, il reste ensuite l’homme fort de son parti, malgré des sanctions américaines pour corruption en 2023.
bio.en: A businessman whose fortune came largely from tobacco, he entered politics late and brought the Colorado Party back to power in 2013. President until 2018, he remained his party's dominant figure despite US corruption sanctions in 2023.
